title: Zoledronic acid · adjuvant · every 6 months

scope.text: Adjuvant breast cancer in an endocrine-depleted setting; confirm natural menopause or the prescribed ovarian suppression/depletion plan.

schedule.dose: 4 mg IV, adjusted for kidney function when required
schedule.infusion: 100 mL sodium chloride 0.9% over at least 15 minutes
schedule.duration: Up to 5 years, or earlier for progression or unacceptable toxicity
schedule.display_warning: Use calendar-month language. The legacy 182-day model is an approximation, not an exact booking interval. Do not invent a fixed total number of doses from the source duration.

patient_purpose.text: This medicine slows the cells that break down bone. In selected people with early breast cancer and low oestrogen levels, it may also reduce the chance of cancer returning in bone. It supports the wider cancer plan rather than replacing surgery, radiotherapy, hormone treatment or chemotherapy.

patient_why.text: Your team weighs the possible benefit against your own recurrence risk, kidney function, dental health and preferences. It is given infrequently, but checks before each infusion and reporting symptoms between visits remain important.

patient_agents.name: Zoledronic acid
patient_agents.alias: An IV infusion approximately every 6 months
patient_agents.explanation: Attaches to mineral in bone and reduces bone breakdown by osteoclasts. The treatment can lower blood calcium, which is why replacement and blood tests matter.
risks: Flu-like symptoms and muscle/joint aches after infusion
Low calcium or other mineral disturbances
Rare thigh/femur fracture and eye inflammation
Allergic reaction; report new palpitations or breathing symptoms

body_map.label: Mouth / jaw
body_map.text: Tell the team about loose teeth, jaw pain or sores that do not heal. Coordinate dental procedures before the next infusion.

body_map.label: Kidneys / urine
body_map.text: Report reduced urine, new swelling, vomiting or difficulty staying hydrated. Kidney results are checked before each dose.

body_map.label: Minerals / nerves
body_map.text: Report tingling or cramps. Severe spasms, seizures or fainting need urgent help. Follow the prescribed calcium and vitamin D plan.

body_map.label: Muscles / joints
body_map.text: Aches or flu-like symptoms can start in the first few days. Contact the team if symptoms are severe, persistent or you feel suddenly unwell.

body_map.label: Thigh / hip
body_map.text: Report new thigh, hip or groin pain promptly so a rare stress fracture can be assessed.

body_map.label: Eyes
body_map.text: New eye pain, redness with pain or a change in vision needs prompt clinical advice.

baseline.text: FBC, renal and liver profile; calcium, phosphate and magnesium. Assess dental risk and arrange examination/preventive care when indicated. Confirm the adjuvant and off-label treatment discussion.

every_infusion.text: Renal profile plus calcium, phosphate and magnesium before each infusion. Compare current creatinine with the treatment baseline and review any previous renal hold.

as_indicated.text: Vitamin D testing and dental review follow clinical need. DEXA and other breast follow-up checks depend on the separate endocrine, bone-health and cancer plan.

cardiac.text: No routine serial echo is specified by this regimen. Fluid-overload risk changes hydration planning; new palpitations, fainting, chest or breathing symptoms require assessment.

after_treatment.text: Keep dental and medical teams informed about previous bisphosphonate exposure and report persistent jaw, thigh or other concerning symptoms. Cancer follow-up follows the wider treatment plan.

support.risk: Minimal service antiemetic classification; NCCP v3 removed the emetogenic-potential section

premedication.text: NCCP specifies no routine premedication. Do not add a chemotherapy steroid, antihistamine or routine antiemetic prescription to this single-agent support plan.

medicines.name: Calcium
medicines.timing: Daily throughout the prescribed support period
medicines.note: Verify the formulation, total intake and renal/electrolyte context; hypercalcaemia is an exception requiring review.

medicines.name: Vitamin D
medicines.timing: Daily throughout the prescribed support period
medicines.note: The prescriber may individualise replacement after vitamin D assessment; hypercalcaemia changes the routine plan.

hydration.text: Maintain appropriate hydration around infusion. The team individualises advice for kidney disease or heart failure; avoid a blanket fluid volume.

dental.text: Use the patient reminder card, maintain oral hygiene and regular dental care, and discuss invasive procedures with oncology and dentistry. No universal drug-holiday interval is established.

interactions.text: Review duplicate bisphosphonates, nephrotoxic medicines, medicines that lower calcium and antiangiogenic treatment.

core: Adjuvant aim and individual expected benefit
Jaw healing / dental procedures and rare atypical fracture
Post-infusion symptoms, allergy and urgent contact advice
Pregnancy/breastfeeding exclusion and relevant contraception discussion

urgent.text: Seek urgent help for severe breathing difficulty, collapse, seizures or a severe allergic reaction. Contact the team promptly for suddenly feeling unwell, reduced urine, severe cramps, new eye symptoms or dental/jaw problems. Do not automatically attribute fever to the expected post-infusion reaction.

implementation_notes: Keep this agent distinct from cytotoxic chemotherapy in patient wording and body-map labels.
Do not add a neutropenia nadir graph, routine hair-loss warning or taxane steroid plan.
In the date-free graph, show infusion, possible early post-infusion reaction and the longer interval to the next planned infusion. Symptoms can arise at any time.
No patient-entered dates or disease-recurrence percentages.
